P1 — PF density sign — Counterevidence: Active diffusion_utils.py:178-209 uses the correct sign. Appendix D.3 Eq.(20) has a path/density sign inconsistency and is not positive counterevidence.

P1 — PF density sign — Counterevidence: The active nonmolecular PF path uses the consistent sign. Fresh inspection of the physical p.19 image shows Eq.(20) is not valid positive counterevidence as previously stated: the displayed path has a minus before integral from 1 to t, hence xdot=-f_tilde, while its density identity uses the sign appropriate to xdot=+f_tilde. The report now records this inconsistency instead of claiming the whole pair is correct.
P2 — W1 returned as W2 in data branch — Counterevidence: Current commit not authenticated as historical experiment commit; no claim of actual benchmark reversal

P2 — W1 returned as W2 in data branch — Counterevidence: The release has separate 1D and SE(3) branches, not covered by this specific proof. Current commit and plotted W2 labels do not establish historical experiment provenance; no actual benchmark reversal follows from the synthetic example.
P3 — TVD drops out-of-range generated mass — Counterevidence: Paper discloses energy-histogram limitations and exclusions; historical magnitude unmeasured

P3 — TVD drops out-of-range generated mass — Counterevidence: Energy histograms cannot identify full state-space distributions, which the report already distinguishes. The 2D implementation uses combined ranges, so this conclusion is limited to the 1D branch. Appendix B exclusion of undefined runs does not recover discarded finite outliers.
P4 — MMD convention mismatch — Counterevidence: MMD squared is legitimate if labeled; fixed-kernel nonnegative ranking preserved

P4 — MMD convention mismatch — Counterevidence: Squared MMD is a legitimate labeled statistic, and for a common fixed kernel its nonnegative population ranking agrees with MMD. A data-dependent bandwidth changes the common-kernel premise, so no universal cross-run ranking statement is made.
